note: Opt-in threat model for non-chapter runs. Legacy runs keep firstStage.rule.incoming 0.44, the def*0.08 term and the viewport-derived spawn ring; this table is read only when a run selects rules='threat-v2'. Two groups. (1) Contact model, R1g-1 / R1g-12: enemyDamage is firstStage.enemies[id].damage * K, and K is the table's only degree of freedom. R1g-1 chose K = 1.8 (the legacy effective contact damage - the 0.82 stage scaler applied - times 2.2) and calibrated it on a driver that R1g-11 then showed to be weaker than the shipped bot: no `f` key, one press a second through the Boss phase, and no warning term. On the rebuilt twin that table reads a 0.147 evolution floor, under G2's 0.25, and the pooled median (0.264) hid it. R1g-12 re-swept K on the twin and landed K = 1.8 * 0.8 = 1.44: the least reduction that puts both journeys inside G2's 25-60% band (classic 0.455, evolution 0.364) while the horde stays lethal to a stationary player (death at 43.8s classic / 37.9s evolution; 74.2s even at K = 0.9). K = 1.62 still misses evolution (0.170), and K = 1.08 already breaches classic's 0.60 ceiling (0.609). The sweep is frozen at tasks/game-remediation/evidence/R1g-12/sweep.json. (2) Boss budget, R1g-3: see src/core/bossBudget.test.ts. bossHp is per journey because the evolved hero brings ~1.8x the Boss DPS, so one shared number cannot put both fights in the GDD's 60-90s window. bossPhaseSpawnInterval and bossDamage are the pressure knobs that make a 60-90s fight survivable: measured before them, the Boss phase killed the player in 30s. spawnRadius and chargeRange exist because both were viewport-derived, which made the standing horde and the Boss charge 46% and 52% larger on a 1280px screen; that alone cost the desktop player 2.5x the HP of the phone player before the Boss even appeared. R1g-7 re-calibrated bossHp twice: the manual dual track added damage (34.5), then reverting D2's dash clamp shortened both fights by ~6s, so both journeys were re-swept at 33 seeds to land inside 60-90s with the 25-60% HP floor intact (classic 15 -> 17.5, evolution 34.5 -> 47.5). (3) Boss move threat, R1g-10: bossDamage is one multiplier on everything the Boss deals, so it cannot buy G4's 15%-per-move target - at the 14.31x that target needs, body contact alone is 82 HP every 1.1s and kills the player inside 10s, before the (correctly delayed) first cast lands. bossSkillDamage and bossContactDamage split that knob, and bossCastCooldown is the cadence half of DECISIONS D7 path A: a multiplier on every fresh cast cooldown (spawn, phase change, recurring), i.e. the same aggregate paid in fewer, bigger moves. All three ship at 1, byte-identical to the R1g-9 reference. (4) Landed cadence, R1g-11: bossCastCooldown and bossSkillDamage are both 14.31, which is the multiple that puts the weakest move (蛮王冲锋 at phase 1) at 15.00% of max HP; bossHp is x1.14 (classic 17.5 -> 19.95, evolution 47.5 -> 54.15) because concentrating the aggregate shortens the fight and G3 wants 60-90s. bossContactDamage is 0.8, not 1: R1g-10 reserved it and R1g-11 needed it. Once every move is avoided, body contact is the Boss's entire remaining damage, and at 1.0 the HP floor of a player who reads the HUD lands at 0.240 on this table (0.232 at R1g-10's hp x 1.1) - under G2's 0.25. These numbers are read on the `hud` arm of bossThreat.test.ts, the twin of tests/settlement.spec.ts: it reads the rendered 首领招式 readout and presses 闪避, never telegraph geometry. Read on a bot that cannot dodge the same table gives hpMin 0 and a ~41% win rate, which is intended - the Boss is now worth dodging. See tasks/game-remediation/evidence/R1g-11/. One caveat, because the pooled median hides it: split by journey the same run reads classic hpMin 0.280 and evolution 0.147, i.e. evolution is under G2. The cause is not the Boss - zeroing enemyDamage lifts evolution to 0.839 and 33 of 33 wins while the Boss's own share stays at 137-175 HP a run. It is the horde contact table below, calibrated on a weaker driver, and it is queued as R1g-12.
